title_en: PICC Property and Casualty Company Limited, Zhongshan Branch v. China Pacific Property Insurance Co., Ltd., Dongguan Branch, et al. — dispute over property insurance contract
keywords_en: Civil; Dispute over property insurance contract; First instance; Intermediate People's Court; Guangdong Province; Legal person; Financial institution; Insurance Law; Elements of double insurance; Exercise of contribution claim right; Effect of third party as insured; Double insurance; Typhoon loss; Fertilizer storage; Insurance compensation; Contribution recovery; Contract dispute; Insurance contract; Guarantee; Dispute over property insurance contract of branch, etc.
full_text_en:
PICC Property and Casualty Company Limited, Zhongshan Branch v. China Pacific Property Insurance Co., Ltd., Dongguan Branch, et al. — dispute over property insurance contract

Case Summary

Under double insurance, where the insurer that has already paid the indemnity is entitled to a claim for contribution, it may seek recourse against other insurers to the extent of their unfulfilled share for the portion of the insurance compensation actually paid in excess of its own share. The insurer that has already paid the indemnity, in exercising its right to claim contribution, correspondingly acquires the rights of the insured. Other insurers may assert against the paying insurer any defenses they have against the insured.

Where a property insurance contract designates a third party other than the contracting parties as the insured, and the insurer fails to prove that the third party refused such designation within a reasonable period, the third party's request that the insurer assume liability for compensation as agreed in the insurance contract shall be supported by the people's court.

Plaintiff: PICC Property and Casualty Company Limited, Zhongshan Branch. Domicile: No. 5 Bo'ai Wulu, East District, Zhongshan City, Guangdong Province.
Responsible Person: Liu Lin, General Manager of the Branch.

Defendant: China Pacific Property Insurance Co., Ltd., Dongguan Branch. Domicile: Guantai Avenue, Nancheng District, Dongguan City, Guangdong Province.
Responsible Person: He Xiaodong, General Manager of the Branch.

Third Party: Dongguan Shenchiwan Port Services Co., Ltd. Domicile: Machong New Port West Road, Machong Town, Dongguan City, Guangdong Province.
Legal Representative: Liu Bin, Chairman of the Board.

Third Party: Dongguan Shenchiwan Terminal Co., Ltd. Domicile: Machong New Port West Road, Machong Town, Dongguan City, Guangdong Province.
Legal Representative: Liu Bin, Chairman of the Board.

The plaintiff, PICC Property and Casualty Company Limited, Zhongshan Branch (hereinafter referred to as "PICC Zhongshan Branch"), initiated an action with the Guangzhou Maritime Court in connection with a dispute over a property insurance contract against the defendant, China Pacific Property Insurance Co., Ltd., Dongguan Branch (hereinafter referred to as "CPIC Dongguan Branch"), and the third parties, Dongguan Shenchiwan Port Services Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Shenchiwan Port Services") and Dongguan Shenchiwan Terminal Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Shenchiwan Terminal").

Plaintiff's Allegations: The third parties, Shenchiwan Port Services and Shenchiwan Terminal, entered into a *Bulk/Bagged Fertilizer Port Agency Agreement* (hereinafter referred to as the "Port Agency Agreement") with Sinochem Fertilizer Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Sinochem"), pursuant to which Sinochem entrusted Shenchiwan Port Services and Shenchiwan Terminal with the agency services for the discharge, storage, and custody of goods arriving at the port. PICC Zhongshan Branch and CPIC Dongguan Branch respectively issued insurance policies covering fertilizers stored by Sinochem at Shenchiwan Terminal, thereby constituting double insurance. Following the loss of the aforesaid fertilizers due to Typhoon "Mangkhut," PICC Zhongshan Branch paid RMB 43,200,000 to Sinochem. As CPIC Dongguan Branch refused to pay the double insurance contribution of RMB 21,600,000, PICC Zhongshan Branch filed this lawsuit, requesting the court to order CPIC Dongguan Branch to pay PICC Zhongshan Branch RMB 21,600,000 as a double insurance contribution, plus interest thereon (calculated on the principal of RMB 21,600,000 at the one-year Loan Prime Rate (LPR) published by the National Interbank Funding Center from December 11, 2019, until the date of full payment by CPIC Dongguan Branch).

Defendant's Defense: The two insurance policies involved in this case do not satisfy the constitutive requirements for double insurance as stipulated in Article 56, Paragraph 4 of the Insurance Law, as the policyholders, insureds, subject matter of insurance, and insurable interests are not identical. Even if double insurance were established, the third parties, Shenchiwan Port Services and Shenchiwan Terminal, failed to notify CPIC Dongguan Branch of the existence of double insurance, thereby rendering the relevant provisions of the insurance contract concerning double insurance void. The plaintiff, PICC Zhongshan Branch, did not notify CPIC Dongguan Branch to participate in the on-site investigation, and the loss amount determined by the Shenzhen Xincheng United Insurance Surveyors and Adjusters Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch (hereinafter referred to as "Xincheng Adjusters"), engaged by PICC Zhongshan Branch, is not objective. The loss amount should be determined based on the expert opinion of Guangzhou Haijiang Insurance Surveyors and Adjusters Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Haijiang Adjusters"), engaged by CPIC Dongguan Branch, which estimates the loss at only slightly over RMB 11.51 million, with a double insurance contribution ratio of 13.8%. PICC Zhongshan Branch's claim that CPIC Dongguan Branch should contribute RMB 21,600,000 lacks factual and legal basis and should be dismissed.

The third parties, Shenchiwan Port Services and Shenchiwan Terminal, did not submit any submissions, evidence, or opinions on evidence.

Facts Found by the Guangzhou Maritime Court at First Instance:

I. Facts Regarding the Conclusion of the Insurance Contracts in Dispute

On March 19, 2018, the plaintiff, PICC Zhongshan Branch, underwrote a Property All Risks Insurance and related additional risks applied for by Sinochem, issuing Policy No. PQYC201844200000000035 (hereinafter referred to as "Policy 035"). The policy stated: the policyholder and insured were Sinochem; the subject matter of insurance was fertilizer; the sum insured was RMB 4,766,484,670.95, representing the selling price of the goods; the insured value was determined as the market value at the time of loss; the premium rate was 0.6302‰; the co-insured included China National Chemical Corporation (hereinafter referred to as "Sinochem Group"), Sinochem Fertilizer Macau Offshore Commercial Services Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Sinochem Macau"), and others; the scope of insurance covered all commodities for which the insured held title; the deductible was the greater of RMB 100,000 or 5% of the loss amount per accident.

In May 2018, the defendant, CPIC Dongguan Branch, won the bid for a package insurance project of the third parties, Shenchiwan Port Services and Shenchiwan Terminal, including a Port Property All Risks Insurance clause and related additional risks. The Port Property All Risks Insurance clause of China Pacific Property Insurance Co., Ltd. stated: insurable property included property under the management or custody of the insured, or property held in trust by the insured, among others; the insured value of the subject matter could be the replacement value at the time of loss, the book balance at the time of loss, the market value at the time of loss, or other values, as agreed between the policyholder and the insurer and specified in the insurance contract; upon becoming aware of an insured event, the insured was required to immediately notify the insurer; if intentional or grossly negligent delay in notification made it difficult to determine the nature, cause, or extent of the loss, the insurer would not be liable for the portion that could not be determined, unless the insurer had already or should have already become aware of the insured event through other channels; if double insurance existed, the insurer would bear liability for compensation in proportion to the sum insured under this insurance contract relative to the total sum insured under this and other insurance contracts. The insurer would not be obligated to advance the compensation amount payable by other insurers. If the insured's failure to disclose truthfully resulted in the insurer overpaying compensation, the insurer was entitled to recover the overpaid portion from the insured. Policy No. ADNGGCZ02418Q000023M (hereinafter referred to as "Policy 23M") stated: the insured were Shenchiwan Port Services/Shenchiwan Terminal and other interested parties; the insured premises included locations such as the Machong Port Area of Humen Port, Dongguan; the subject matter of insurance included: 1. Buildings and ancillary facilities, 2. Mechanical and electrical equipment and ancillary equipment, 3. Marine structures, 4. Inventory (including inventory owned by the insured and inventory owned by third parties under the insured's operations/custody); the owners of the extended inventory were co-insured; the sum insured for inventory was determined based on the book balance, amounting to RMB 2,469,750,000, and was recognized as insured to full value; the premium rate was 0.3‰; the premium was RMB 740,925; the absolute deductible per accident for property losses caused by typhoon was the greater of RMB 50,000 or 20% of the loss amount; a replacement value clause stipulated that if the policyholder and the insurer agreed that the insured value would be the replacement value at the time of loss, and in the event of loss where double insurance existed and other insurance contracts did not underwrite on a replacement value basis, the insured value would be changed to the market value at the time of loss.

II. Facts Regarding the Sale, Storage, Loss, Inspection, Survey, and Disposal of the Goods in Dispute

On January 11, 2017, Sinochem, and the third parties, Shenchiwan Port Services and Shenchiwan Terminal, entered into the *Port Agency Agreement*, stipulating that Shenchiwan Port Services and Shenchiwan Terminal would provide relevant agency services for bulk/bagged fertilizers shipped to their port/port area by Sinochem, and that Sinochem would be responsible for insuring the goods during storage at the port.

Evidence from the plaintiff, PICC Zhongshan Branch, showed: Sinochem Group purchased from Sinochem Macau various fertilizers, including Canadian red potassium chloride, Jordanian potassium chloride, Belgian compound fertilizer (hereinafter referred to as "Befu"), and Norwegian compound fertilizer; Sinochem and Sinochem Fertilizer Co., Ltd., Hainan Branch, purchased from Yara Trading (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. 300 tons of calcium ammonium nitrate and 4,500 tons of Norwegian compound fertilizer. The aforementioned fertilizers were stored and stacked in the port area of Shenchiwan Port Services and Shenchiwan Terminal in Machong. According to the statistics of Shenchiwan Port Services and Shenchiwan Terminal, as of September 16, 2018, a total of 308,333.68 tons of various fertilizers belonging to Sinochem were stacked at the terminal.

At approximately 17:00 on September 16, 2018, Typhoon "Mangkhut" made landfall in Haiyan Town, Jiangmen, Guangdong, with a central wind force of approximately Category 14, causing tidal surges in the Shenchiwan Port area of Dongguan's Machong Port to flow inland, damaging the fertilizers stacked at the Machong terminal at the bottom layer and under partially torn tarpaulins. Following the accident, Sinochem claimed losses of RMB 57,884,179.24 from PICC Zhongshan Branch. PICC Zhongshan Branch engaged Xincheng Adjusters to conduct on-site investigations and loss assessments. Xincheng Adjusters conducted on-site inspections and sampling, and the samples were tested by Anhui Jingwei Testing Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Jingwei"). Ultimately, Xincheng Adjusters determined that Sinochem suffered a loss of RMB 43,427,337.88 due to the accident in question, with an adjusted amount of RMB 43,203,058.34.

On December 2, 2019, PICC Zhongshan Branch sent a letter to CPIC Dongguan Branch, stating that both parties should each bear 50% of the compensation liability under the double insurance, and that PICC Zhongshan Branch intended to pay Sinochem a full indemnity of RMB 43,200,000, after which CPIC Dongguan Branch would pay PICC Zhongshan Branch RMB 21,600,000. If CPIC Dongguan Branch intended to pay Sinochem directly, it was requested to notify PICC Zhongshan Branch within three days of receiving the letter. CPIC Dongguan Branch acknowledged receipt but did not reply. On December 10, 2019, PICC Zhongshan Branch paid insurance compensation of RMB 43,200,000 to Sinochem. Thereafter, PICC Zhongshan Branch again sent a letter to CPIC Dongguan Branch, stating that PICC Zhongshan Branch had fully paid Sinochem RMB 43,200,000, and requesting that CPIC Dongguan Branch pay PICC Zhongshan Branch 50% of the insurance compensation, i.e., RMB 21,600,000. This letter was also acknowledged by CPIC Dongguan Branch.

During the first instance proceedings, CPIC Dongguan Branch engaged Haijiang Adjusters to provide analysis opinions on the survey report of Xincheng Adjusters and to conduct an assessment of the fertilizer loss accident in question. Haijiang Adjusters opined that the Xincheng Adjusters' report had serious issues regarding the qualifications of the sampling company, sampling methods, sampling procedures, and on-site inspections, and that the loss assessment was significantly overstated. Haijiang Adjusters determined that the insured value of the 308,333.68 tons of various fertilizers in question was RMB 763,155,321.09, with a total loss amount of RMB 10,393,321. They calculated CPIC Dongguan Branch's liability ratio at 13.8%, resulting in a compensation amount of RMB 1,147,422.64.

To dispose of the damaged fertilizers in question, PICC Zhongshan Branch sent invitations to relevant companies and organized on-site inspections. Relevant companies sent offer letters to PICC Zhongshan Branch, and part of the damaged fertilizers was sold at auction. Guangzhou Wancheng Appraisal & Real Estate and Land Valuation Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Wancheng") issued an asset appraisal report on the market unit prices of the damaged fertilizers, stating that the appraisal base date was September 16, 2018, the value type was market value, the appraisal method was the market approach, and providing the unit prices for various types of fertilizers.

Opinion of the Guangzhou Maritime Court at First Instance:

This case involves a dispute over contribution for double insurance. The issues at first instance were: whether double insurance existed; whether the plaintiff, PICC Zhongshan Branch, was entitled to claim contribution; whether PICC Zhongshan Branch's payment of indemnity was reasonable and prudent; and the reasonable amount of contribution to be borne by the defendant, CPIC Dongguan Branch.

I. Whether Double Insurance Existed

Both insurance contracts in dispute were legally valid. PICC Zhongshan Branch and CPIC Dongguan Branch were different insurers under different insurance contracts. The subject matter of insurance under Policy 035 included fertilizers, pesticides, and other goods in which Sinochem, Sinochem Group, and other insureds held an insurable interest, stored at various ports and inland storage yards and warehouses across China. The subject matter of insurance under Policy 23M included, among multiple insured premises including the Machong Port Area, "inventory owned by the insured and inventory owned by third parties under the insured's operations/custody." Accordingly, the 308,333.68 tons of various fertilizers belonging to Sinochem, stored in the Machong Port Area and under the operations/supervision of the third parties, Shenchiwan Port Services and Shenchiwan Terminal (hereinafter referred to as "Sinochem's fertilizers stacked in the Machong Port Area"), fell within the overlapping scope of the subject matter of insurance under both policies, constituting the "same subject matter of insurance." Both insurance contracts extended coverage to co-insureds. Sinochem, which held an insurable interest under Policy 035, also qualified as an insured under Policy 23M as a "cargo owner" with an extended insurable interest. Moreover, Sinochem's insurable interest in the fertilizers under both policies was identical. Sinochem was unaware of Policy 23M at the time of taking out the insurance and at the time of the insured accident; therefore, it could not be found to have breached its duty to notify of double insurance. Considering that both policies satisfied the other constitutive requirements for double insurance under Article 56, Paragraph 4 of the Insurance Law—namely, the "same insured event," being within the insurance period, the sum of the sums insured exceeding the insured value of the subject matter, and the absence of a "prohibition on other insurance" clause—the two policies in dispute constituted double insurance.

II. Whether PICC Zhongshan Branch Was Entitled to Claim Contribution

The Policy 23M did not contain a "no contribution clause," and PICC Zhongshan Branch and CPIC Dongguan Branch did not agree to prohibit contribution after the accident occurred. Given that the insurance compensation paid by PICC Zhongshan Branch did not exceed the insured value of the subject matter, in accordance with Article 56, Paragraph 2 of the Insurance Law, PICC Zhongshan Branch was entitled to request contribution of the insurance compensation from CPIC Dongguan Branch.

III. Whether PICC Zhongshan Branch's Payment of Indemnity Was Reasonable and Prudent

This case is a civil dispute, and the standard of proof required for PICC Zhongshan Branch to establish the relevant facts supporting its claim is merely the "high probability" standard. Given the significant impact of Typhoon "Mangkhut," the inspection and sampling of damaged goods in the port area must take into account the objective circumstances on-site. Since Sinochem was unaware of the double insurance, Xincheng Adjusters' inspection and sampling were conducted with the consent of both PICC Zhongshan Branch and Sinochem. Even if sampling did not achieve full coverage, the description of the inspection site and the selection of samples were reasonable, and the testing of samples was completed by Jingwei, which possesses relevant professional testing qualifications. This case is not a dispute over the inspection and appraisal of import/export commodities, and the law does not explicitly require that the determination of losses for damaged fertilizers must be carried out by inspection and appraisal institutions as stipulated in the *Administrative Measures for Import and Export Commodity Inspection and Appraisal Institutions*. Therefore, Xincheng Adjusters' survey opinion regarding the extent of fertilizer damage is consistent with the objective damage situation with a "high probability." Even if Xincheng Adjusters' estimation of the market value of some damaged fertilizers was too high, PICC Zhongshan Branch ultimately based its payment on the prices of the relevant fertilizers declared by Sinochem when applying for insurance. Consequently, its actual payment of RMB 43,200,000 was not manifestly improper.

IV. The Reasonable Amount of Contribution to Be Borne by CPIC Dongguan Branch

Pursuant to the special provisions clause of Policy 23M, if double insurance exists and other insurance contracts do not underwrite on a replacement value basis, the insured value of the subject matter is changed to the market value at the time of loss. Since Policy 23M did not explicitly stipulate the insured value of the fertilizers, CPIC Dongguan Branch should calculate its contribution based on the actual market value of the damaged fertilizers. According to Article 56, Paragraph 2 of the Insurance Law, CPIC Dongguan Branch's contribution liability should be determined in proportion to its sum insured relative to the total sum insured. Given that the fertilizers belonging to Sinochem stacked in the Machong Port Area constituted the overlapping portion of the subject matter of insurance under both policies and were insured to full value under both, PICC Zhongshan Branch and CPIC Dongguan Branch should share the contribution on a 50% basis. Policy 23M stipulated that the absolute deductible per accident for property losses caused by typhoon was the greater of RMB 50,000 or 20% of the loss amount. Accordingly, the contribution amount payable by CPIC Dongguan Branch was RMB 17,280,000 [43,200,000 × 50% × (1 - 20%) = 17,280,000]. Since CPIC Dongguan Branch delayed payment of the aforementioned amount, it should pay PICC Zhongshan Branch corresponding interest calculated on the principal amount.

In conclusion, pursuant to Article 12, Paragraphs 2, 5, and 6, Article 56, Paragraphs 2 and 4 of the Insurance Law, and Article 108, Paragraph 1 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, on November 4, 2020, the Guangzhou Maritime Court rendered the following judgment:

The defendant, China Pacific Property Insurance Co., Ltd., Dongguan Branch, shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, pay to the plaintiff, PICC Property and Casualty Company Limited, Zhongshan Branch, the double insurance contribution amount of RMB 17,280,000, plus interest thereon (calculated on the principal of RMB 17,280,000 at the one-year Loan Prime Rate (LPR) published by the National Interbank Funding Center from December 11, 2019, until the date of full payment by CPIC Dongguan Branch).

CPIC Dongguan Branch, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Guangdong High People's Court.

Taibao Dongguan Branch stated in its appeal: 1. There is no overlapping insurance in this case. The same subject matter insured must be a completely identical subject matter and cannot be divided. Even if the scope of the subject matter insured under the two insurance contracts partially overlaps, it does not satisfy the condition of the same subject matter insured. The insurable interests of Sinochem and the third parties at first instance, Shenchiwan Port Company and Shenchiwan Dock Company, under the two insurance contracts arise from different rights, and thus the two insurances in this case do not share the same insurable interest, as evidenced by the different claims settlement results. The cargo owner under the two insurance contracts is a co-insured and an insured respectively, and the concepts and connotations of the two are fundamentally different. According to the Port Agency Agreement and the fact that Sinochem took out insurance, the inventory under the 23M insurance contract does not include Sinochem's goods. Taibao Dongguan Branch may, based on the principle of privity of contract, decline to process Sinochem's claim. Moreover, Sinochem only owns the calcium ammonium nitrate and Norwegian compound fertilizer stored at Machong Port. 2. Even if overlapping insurance exists, the appellee PICC Zhongshan Branch has no right to claim contribution. Both insurance contracts state that the insurer is not responsible for advancing compensation payable by other insurers. PICC Zhongshan Branch can only recover the overpaid amount from the insured. 3. Xincheng Public Adjuster seriously inflated the loss assessment amount. The total loss amount of the accident should be determined as RMB 10,393,321 based on the expert opinion of Haijiang Public Adjuster. The 035 insurance contract did not specify that the goods were fully insured. The contribution ratio of Taibao Dongguan Branch is 13.8%, and the contribution amount is RMB 1,147,422.64. In summary, [Taibao Dongguan Branch] requests that the first-instance judgment be reversed and PICC Zhongshan Branch's claims be dismissed in the amended judgment.

The appellee PICC Zhongshan Branch responded: 1. PICC Zhongshan Branch is entitled to claim contribution for overlapping insurance from the appellant Taibao Dongguan Branch. PICC Zhongshan Branch previously sent a notice to Taibao Dongguan Branch requesting joint compensation, but Taibao Dongguan Branch did not respond. To protect the legitimate rights and interests of Sinochem, PICC Zhongshan Branch waived its right not to advance compensation, but this does not affect its claim for contribution. 2. The two insurances in this case constitute overlapping insurance. The overlapping part of the subject matter insured under multiple insurance contracts belongs to the same subject matter insured. Sinochem is the owner of the fertilizers in question, and the "cargo owner" under the 23M insurance contract includes the owner and any entity that has established legal relationships such as port operation agency with the third parties at first instance, Shenchiwan Port Company and Shenchiwan Dock Company, regarding that inventory. Sinochem is an insured under both insurances and has the same insurable interest in the subject matter insured. The sameness of the insurance claims settlement amount is not a constituent element of overlapping insurance. 3. Both insurance contracts provide full insurance for the inventory. Taibao Dongguan Branch and PICC Zhongshan Branch should share the compensation in equal proportions. 4. When handling the related insurance accident, Taibao Dongguan Branch did not inspect the accident site, did not send personnel to participate in the loss assessment after receiving notice, and did not raise objections after receiving the adjuster’s report. This should be deemed as Taibao Dongguan Branch waiving its right to verify the loss of the insured accident. The first-instance court’s determination that PICC Zhongshan Branch could pay RMB 43,200,000 to Sinochem based on the degree of fertilizer damage determined by Xincheng Public Adjuster was not improper. In summary, [PICC Zhongshan Branch] requests that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment be upheld.

The third parties at first instance, Shenchiwan Port Company and Shenchiwan Dock Company, did not submit any opinions.

During the second instance, the appellant Taibao Dongguan Branch submitted the following evidence: 1. The "Property All Risks Insurance" of PICC Property and Casualty Company Limited used in the 035 insurance contract, purportedly to prove that the appellee PICC Zhongshan Branch has no right to claim contribution; 2. The national standards for potassium chloride, urea, and compound fertilizers, purportedly to prove that the loss amount determined by Xincheng Public Adjuster was unreasonable. The Guangdong High People's Court, based on PICC Zhongshan Branch’s opinions on the evidence, confirmed the authenticity and legality of the evidence submitted by Taibao Dongguan Branch. Article 32 of the "Property All Risks Insurance" provides: "At the time of an insured accident, if overlapping insurance exists, the insurer shall bear compensation liability in proportion to the corresponding sum insured under this insurance contract to the total sum insured under other insurance contracts and this insurance contract. The insurer shall not be responsible for advancing the compensation amount payable by other insurers. If the insured fails to truthfully disclose information, causing the insurer to overpay compensation, the insurer shall have the right to recover the overpaid portion from the insured." The probative force of the two pieces of evidence needs to be determined in conjunction with other evidence in this case.

The appellee PICC Zhongshan Branch submitted the following evidence: the "Letter from Sinochem Group Regarding the Ownership of Goods of Sinochem Fertilizer Co., Ltd." and translations of English materials such as sales contracts submitted at first instance, purportedly to prove that Sinochem is the owner of the fertilizers in question. The Guangdong High People's Court, based on the appellant Taibao Dongguan Branch’s opinions on the evidence, confirmed the authenticity of the letter. The content of the letter is: Sinochem Group, acting as an agent, imported fertilizers for Sinochem. After import, the goods stored at Shenchiwan Dock Company had all been delivered to Sinochem, and Sinochem owned the aforementioned goods. Sinochem has the right to possess, use, control, and dispose of the aforementioned goods. The goods damaged at Shenchiwan Dock Company due to Typhoon Mangkhut were all disposed of by Sinochem, and Sinochem received the corresponding insurance compensation. The probative force of the two pieces of evidence needs to be determined in conjunction with other evidence in this case.

It was additionally found that the survey report issued by Xincheng Public Adjuster stated that potash fertilizer and urea were fully insured, while compound fertilizer was not fully insured; the insurance ratio = insured quantity / balance quantity × 100%; the residual value of the goods was RMB 0, and the deductible was RMB 0.

The Guangdong High People's Court, after the second instance, confirmed the facts found by the first-instance court except for the fact that the compound fertilizer was fully insured under the 035 insurance contract.

The Guangdong High People's Court held in the second instance as follows:

This case is a dispute over contribution for overlapping insurance under property insurance contracts. The issues in dispute in the second instance are: 1. Whether the insurances in this case constitute overlapping insurance; 2. If they constitute overlapping insurance, whether the appellee PICC Zhongshan Branch’s claim for contribution is established; 3. If the claim for contribution is established, how should PICC Zhongshan Branch exercise it.

I. Whether the insurances in this case constitute overlapping insurance

According to Article 56(4) of the Insurance Law, the constituent elements of overlapping insurance include: multiple valid insurance contracts, the same insured, the same subject matter insured, the same insurable interest, the same insured event, different insurers, and the total sum insured exceeding the insured value, among others. During the second instance, the dispute between the parties as to whether the two insurances in this case constitute overlapping insurance with respect to Sinochem’s fertilizers stored at Machong Port area mainly focuses on whether the elements of "the same insured," "the same subject matter insured," and "the same insurable interest" are satisfied.

(1) Whether the element of "the same insured" is satisfied

Both parties have no dispute that Sinochem is the insured under the 035 insurance contract. The appellant Taibao Dongguan Branch contends that Sinochem is not the insured under the 23M insurance contract, primarily on the grounds that Sinochem is not the "cargo owner," that the "co-insured" is not equivalent to the "insured," and that Sinochem has no right to claim compensation from Taibao Dongguan Branch by breaking through the privity of contract. "Cargo owner" is not a legal concept but a commercial term appearing in the insurance policy, and its interpretation should be consistent with commercial transaction practices and common understanding. The fertilizers stored by Sinochem at Machong Port area are movables, and the rules of rights applicable to them in commercial transactions should reflect the transferability of movables and maintain the predictability of commercial order. Because Sinochem possesses, uses, and enjoys, in whole or in part, the rights of usufruct over the fertilizers stored at Machong Port area in commercial transactions, it is considered the "cargo owner." The 23M insurance policy does not specify the meaning of "co-insured." Confirming that the "co-insured" enjoys the rights ordinarily enjoyed by an insured and is not an additional insured is more conducive to protecting the legitimate rights of the insured. The 23M insurance contract stipulates that the cargo owner of the inventory is the insured, which falls under the circumstance where a third party other than the parties to the insurance contract is designated as the insured. Accordingly, the third party may, without paying insurance premiums, spread the property losses it may suffer through insurance as a method of risk sharing. This clause is a third-party beneficiary clause. Regarding the effect of a third-party beneficiary clause on a third party, Article 522(2) of the Civil Code provides that where the law or the agreement of the parties allows the third party to exercise the right to demand performance from the debtor, and the third party does not expressly refuse it within a reasonable period, the third party may request the debtor to assume liability for breach of contract. This is a newly added provision of the Civil Code. The 23M insurance contract was entered into before the implementation of the Civil Code, and the law applicable at that time did not provide for the effect of third-party beneficiary clauses on third parties. Applying Article 522(2) of the Civil Code to this case is consistent with the mutual agreement of the parties as recorded in the contract, reflects the consideration relationship between the cargo owner and the third parties at first instance, Shenchiwan Port Company and Shenchiwan Dock Company. It both protects the legitimate interests of the cargo owner as an insured while granting it the right to waive, and both confirms the insurer's right to raise defenses while imposing corresponding burdens of proof. This complies with the conditions for applying newly added provisions of the Civil Code as stipulated in Article 3 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Temporal Effect of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China. According to this article of the Civil Code, Sinochem does not need to express its intention to accept the agreement; as long as it does not expressly refuse within a reasonable period, it is deemed the insured. The appellant Taibao Dongguan Branch argues that by not claiming against it, Sinochem has admitted it is not the insured. However, the evidence adduced is insufficient to prove that Sinochem expressly refused to be the insured within a reasonable period. Therefore, this argument does not stand. Accordingly, Sinochem is the insured under both insurances in this case, and the two insurances satisfy the element of "the same insured."

(2) Whether the elements of "the same subject matter insured" and "the same insurable interest" are satisfied

The fertilizers stored by Sinochem at Machong Port area are the overlapping part of the scope of property covered under the two insurances in this case. They can be physically and economically separated from other covered property, and neither the law nor the insurance contracts prohibit such separation. Therefore, these fertilizers and the interests therein constitute the "same subject matter insured" under the two insurances. Sinochem enjoys the same insurable interest in these fertilizers under both insurance contracts. Although the claims settlement results of the two insurances may differ due to factors such as insured value, sum insured, deductible, extent of damage, market value, etc., these differences are insufficient to deny the identity of the insurable interest. Accordingly, the two insurances in this case satisfy the elements of "the same subject matter insured" and "the same insurable interest."

II. Whether the appellee PICC Zhongshan Branch’s claim for contribution is established

To determine whether the appellee PICC Zhongshan Branch’s claim for contribution is established, it is necessary first to examine whether an insurer that has already paid compensation has a right to contribution for overlapping insurance, and then to determine whether PICC Zhongshan Branch’s claim for contribution in this case is established.

(1) Whether an insurer that has already paid compensation has a right to contribution for overlapping insurance

The right to contribution for overlapping insurance refers to the right of an insurer that has already paid compensation, under overlapping insurance, to recover from other insurers that have not fulfilled or have only partially fulfilled their insurance compensation obligations (i.e., non-paying insurers) the portion of the actual insurance compensation paid that exceeds its own share. Article 56 of the Insurance Law only specifies the method for determining the proportion of liability of each insurer under overlapping insurance but does not clearly provide for a right to contribution. The reasons for confirming that an insurer that has already paid compensation enjoys a right to contribution for overlapping insurance are as follows:

First, Article 56 of the Insurance Law is a provision on the standard for determining the internal liability proportions among insurers and does not prohibit an insurer from paying insurance compensation exceeding its proportion of liability when actually settling claims. Article 59 of the Insurance Law provides that an insurer that has paid all or part of the sum insured acquires all or part of the rights to the damaged subject matter insured. In property insurance, the rights to the damaged subject matter insured that vest in the insurer are property rights, including the creditor's right of the insured to demand payment of insurance compensation from the insurer. Although this creditor's right is extinguished upon payment, the law fictitiously deems the creditor's right to continue to exist and to be acquired by the paying insurer, which is entitled to assert it against non-paying insurers.

Second, overlapping insurance originated in marine insurance. Marine insurance and general property insurance share commonalities in the theoretical basis, balancing of interests, and proportion of liability concerning overlapping insurance. Article 225 of the Maritime Law of the People's Republic of China provides that under overlapping insurance, an insurer that has already paid compensation has the right to recover from non-paying insurers. This is a clear provision on the internal allocation of liability among insurers and can serve as a basis for the legitimacy of the right to contribution for overlapping insurance in general insurance.

Finally, overlapping insurance is a derivative system of the principle of indemnity in insurance. Its legislative purpose is not only to permit the insured to obtain insurance protection from multiple policies without receiving duplicate compensation, but also to balance the interests among different insurers and to encourage insurers to assume insurance liability. An insurer that has already paid compensation and overpays the insured relieves other insurers of their corresponding compensation liability. Confirming that such an insurer enjoys a right to contribution reflects the principle of balancing interests and affirms the proactive compensation behavior of insurers. This helps simplify the claims process for the insured, reduces claims costs, better realizes the institutional value of insurance in spreading risks and enhancing protection, encourages insurers to actively participate in claims settlement and offer more competitively priced insurance services, promotes the healthy and orderly development of the insurance industry, and fosters a trustworthy and friendly social environment.

(2) Whether the appellee PICC Zhongshan Branch’s claim for contribution is established

Whether a paying insurer's claim for contribution against a non-paying insurer that is the subject of the contribution request is established requires an examination of whether the elements for establishing a contribution claim are satisfied. Among these, the positive elements include: the insurer asserting the contribution claim has performed its insurance liability; the other insurer has been relieved, in whole or in part, of its debt due to the conduct of the paying insurer; and the paying insurer has borne a greater proportion of insurance compensation liability than its share. Negative elements include the absence of any reasons that would preclude the establishment of the contribution claim, among others.

In this case, the appellant Taibao Dongguan Branch did not perform its compensation liability in accordance with the insurance contract. The parties did not agree on the proportion of liability. The liability proportions stipulated in both insurance contracts are the same as those provided in Article 56 of the Insurance Law. Therefore, the parties shall bear compensation liability in proportion to the sum insured under their respective insurance contracts to the total sum insured. The two insurance contracts use the same method for calculating the insured value of the fertilizers. The 23M insurance contract states that the inventory is fully insured, while the 035 insurance contract does not specify this nor does it record the sum insured. The survey report of Xincheng Public Adjuster shows that part of the compound fertilizer was not fully insured under the 035 insurance contract. According to the calculation method for the adjustment amount used in that report, the insurance ratio for Sinochem's fertilizers stored at Machong Port area under the 035 insurance contract was 99.48% (RMB 43,203,058.34 ÷ RMB 43,427,337.88 × 100% = 99.48%). Accordingly, the appellee PICC Zhongshan Branch’s liability ratio under overlapping insurance is 49.87% [99.48 ÷ (99.48 + 100) × 100% = 49.87%]. The first-instance court opined that PICC Zhongshan Branch bore 50% of the liability, which is inconsistent with the fact that Sinochem did not fully insure. The second instance corrects this. PICC Zhongshan Branch actually paid RMB 43,200,000 to Sinochem, which constitutes overpayment of insurance compensation liability. Although both insurance contracts stipulate that the insurer is not responsible for advancing compensation payable by other insurers, neither contract sets forth the prerequisites for payment nor the consequences of overpayment. Therefore, this does not constitute a bar to the paying insurer’s right to contribution. Accordingly, PICC Zhongshan Branch’s claim for contribution against Taibao Dongguan Branch is established.

III. How should the appellee PICC Zhongshan Branch exercise its claim for contribution?

An insurer that has already paid compensation exercising its right to contribution for overlapping insurance shall comply with legal provisions and the agreement of the parties, and reflect the nature of the right itself and the institutional value. In this case, the dispute between the parties regarding how to exercise the contribution claim involves the priority of the contribution claim, the scope of exercise, the corresponding proportion of liability, and the determination of the amount.

(1) The priority of the appellee PICC Zhongshan Branch’s claim for contribution

In overlapping insurance, an insurer that has already paid compensation has different claims against different parties, including: a claim for contribution against non-paying insurers, a right to demand the insured refund overpaid compensation, and a right of subrogation against third parties. In the absence of legal provisions or special agreement by the parties, the appellee PICC Zhongshan Branch has the right to first assert its claim for contribution against the appellant Taibao Dongguan Branch.

(2) The scope of exercise of the appellee PICC Zhongshan Branch’s claim for contribution

The exercise of a right has boundaries. According to Article 59 of the Insurance Law, the scope of exercise of a contribution claim for overlapping insurance is the entirety or part of the insured's right to claim insurance compensation against non-paying insurers and ancillary rights thereto, as well as ancillary rights of the contribution claim itself, excluding rights that cannot be acquired in accordance with legal or agreed conditions. The appellant Taibao Dongguan Branch, arguing that Xincheng Public Adjuster inflated the loss and that the appellee PICC Zhongshan Branch failed to exercise due diligence in review, requests that the unreasonable compensation amount be deducted. In this regard, the first-instance court conducted a careful review and explained in detail the reasons and basis for not supporting Taibao Dongguan Branch’s argument. Although the national standards submitted by Taibao Dongguan Branch during the second instance differ from the survey report of Xincheng Public Adjuster, Taibao Dongguan Branch did not prove that these differences render the survey report obviously erroneous and thus inadmissible. Therefore, its argument for deducting the unreasonable compensation amount is not established.

The scope of the paying insurer’s claim for contribution against a non-paying insurer shall not exceed the scope of the claim that the insured originally had against the non-paying insurer. The non-paying insurer may assert against the paying insurer the same defenses based on deductible items and amounts stipulated in the insurance contract that it could have asserted against the insured. The 23M insurance contract stipulates a deductible of RMB 50,000 or 20% of the loss amount, whichever is higher, for property losses caused by typhoons. The amount of the contribution claim that the appellee PICC Zhongshan Branch is entitled to exercise shall be reduced by this deductible amount.

(3) The proportion of liability corresponding to the appellee PICC Zhongshan Branch’s claim for contribution

The obligation corresponding to a contribution claim for overlapping insurance is a joint obligation by shares among multiple obligors. To avoid circular exercise of contribution claims, the contribution that a paying insurer is entitled to claim against each non-paying insurer shall be limited to the share that each non-paying insurer should have borne. The proportion of liability corresponding to the appellee PICC Zhongshan Branch’s contribution claim shall be determined based on the proportion of the appellant Taibao Dongguan Branch’s insurance compensation liability under overlapping insurance, which is 50.13% [100 ÷ (99.48 + 100) × 100% = 50.13%]. Taibao Dongguan Branch’s argument that the insurer with a larger sum insured and higher premium collected, i.e., PICC Zhongshan Branch, should bear greater compensation liability is inconsistent with legal provisions and the insurance contract, and also conflicts with the characteristic that the economic value of the premium and insurance compensation in a single insurance relationship in property insurance is not equivalent but together ensures the equivalence of the aggregate relationship of property insurance. The court does not support this argument.

(4) The amount corresponding to the appellee PICC Zhongshan Branch’s claim for contribution

The system design of the contribution claim in double insurance is intended to prevent insurers from evading insurance liability, but it also does not allow insurers to obtain additional benefits from it. The amount corresponding to the contribution claim of the insurer that has already paid compensation shall be determined based on the actual amount of compensation paid, combined with the proportion of liability and the deductible amount. In this case, the amount corresponding to the contribution claim of the appellee, PICC Zhongshan Branch, is RMB 17,324,928 [43,200,000 × 50.13% × (1-20%) = 17,324,928]. The first-instance court ordered the appellant, CPIC Dongguan Branch, to pay insurance contribution of RMB 17,280,000, which is lower than the amount claimed by PICC Zhongshan Branch and the amount corresponding to its contribution claim. PICC Zhongshan Branch did not appeal this determination, and the second-instance court upheld this result. Interest is statutory fruits. The first-instance court calculated the interest amount based on RMB 17,280,000 as the principal amount of the contribution, which is lower than the interest amount claimed by PICC Zhongshan Branch and the interest amount calculated based on the amount corresponding to the contribution claim as the principal. PICC Zhongshan Branch did not appeal this determination, and the second-instance court upheld this result. Accordingly, CPIC Dongguan Branch shall pay PICC Zhongshan Branch the double insurance contribution of RMB 17,280,000 and interest thereon (calculated on the principal of RMB 17,280,000, from December 11, 2019, until full repayment, at the loan prime rate (LPR) for one-year loans published by the National Interbank Funding Center).

In summary, although the first-instance court's factual findings had minor flaws, the application of law and the judgment result were generally correct. The second-instance court does not support the appellant CPIC Dongguan Branch's appeal claims. The Guangdong High People's Court, in accordance with Article 177, paragraph 1, item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 334 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, rendered the following judgment on March 15, 2022:

Appeal dismissed; the original judgment is affirmed.
